newsitem.title: USA: US corp bonds up with Treasuries, new issues eyed.
newsitem.headline: US corp bonds up with Treasuries, new issues eyed.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds were trading higher tracking U.S. Treasuries in light trading as players focused in on the new issue arena, dealers said.
"It's been a quiet day with no change in spreads but obviously things are up in tandem with the government market," one high-grade trader said.
High-grade dealers said some two-way trading was seen with a little more emphasis on the buyside.
"There's been a little more customer interest but no significant change from yesterday," one trader said.
"There hasn't been a lot of news nor a lot of trading," said another high-grade trader. "People are more concerned with how the Treasury market is doing so we're just kind of sitting there."
Meanwhile, issuers wanting to take advantage of a dip in Treasury yields stepped into the primary market to issue debt, dealers said.
On Thursday, Anixter Inc priced $100 million seven-year notes to yield 135 basis points over Treasuries via Merrill Lynch & Co, dealers said.
Also, Comerica's priced $150 million in 30-year debt to yield 85 basis points over Treasuries via CS First Boston.
In addition, Associates Corp of North America priced $400 million in three-year notes to yield 26 basis points over U.S. Treasuries via Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
In secondary new issue trading, dealers said Wednesday's yankee debt offerings were well received by the market and met with good demand, dealers said.
European Investment Bank's 10-year global bonds were seen trading at a spread of 17 basis points, where the paper initially priced.
"EAB's issue came at a spread of 17 basis points and has held firm at that level," said another trader.
Australia & New Zealand Banking's 10-year issue via Merrill Lynch & Co was also seen as a very successful debt offering, dealers said.
"ANZ's 10-year deal was very successful and was upped in size to meet investor demand," said one syndicate source.
The bank's 10-year issue was trading at a spread of 64 basis point bid, 63 basis points offered on the break, traders said.
Turning to the junk sector, the broader high-yield market was quoted up 1/4 to 3/8 in tandem with an improved bond and stock market market, dealers said.

In active isues, Rally's Hamburgers 9.875 percent notes due 2000 were up 3-1/2 points at 87-1/4 bid, 87-1/2 offer, but were quoted as much as five points higher in Thursday's session, high-yield traders said.
Rally's said on Thursday it is seeking consent from bondholders to amend the indenture.
Rally's wants the amendment to allow two equity holders to acquire a 35 percent stake in the company without triggering the existing change of control provisions.
These provisions require the company to offer to purchase the senior notes at 101 percent of their face value, Rally's said.
In other issues, Brunos also gained 1/2 a point at 101-3/4 bid, traders added.
In the government market, the benchmark U.S. Treasury bond was trading up 11/32 at 95-28/32 to yield 7.08 percent.
--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675
